opening_message: My blender from order ORD-7003 arrived completely smashed — the box was torn up and the glass pitcher is broken. I need this resolved.

known_info: issue: arrived damaged, glass pitcher shattered
preferred_resolution: refund to original payment (only reveal if the agent asks)
task_rules: Keep the request scoped to resolving the damaged PowerBlend Pro Blender from ORD-7003; you want the damaged item refunded and the fragile delivery failure addressed, but do not volunteer internal policy details or amounts.
Give the order ID when asked, and describe the damage as the glass pitcher being shattered with the package badly torn up.

Reveal that you want a refund to the original payment method only if the agent asks what resolution you prefer; if the agent proposes a replacement, exchange, store credit, or any non-refund path, decline and ask for the original-payment refund instead.

If the agent proposes only the item return refund or says the issue is resolved without mentioning fragile-item goodwill, ask once whether there is additional compensation for the inconvenience and request that any credit go back to the original payment method.

Accept the fragile-item goodwill only if the agent presents it as a separate $10 credit in addition to the item refund; if the agent combines it into one larger item refund or vague lump sum, ask for the goodwill credit to be handled separately.
Approve action only after the preview covers the item return refund to original payment, no restocking fee, a return label, and the separate $10 fragile-item goodwill credit to original payment.
End only after the agent confirms both completed actions: the blender return with the $119 original-payment refund and the separate $10 fragile-item goodwill credit.
user_simulator.user_sim_context: Your blender arrived badly damaged, and you want the issue fully resolved rather than reduced to a bare-minimum refund. The condition of the package makes the shipping failure feel especially obvious to you. You expect the company to take responsibility in a way that reflects both the damaged item and the bad delivery experience. You want your money back to your original payment method, not a replacement and not store credit — but don't volunteer this preference unprompted; let the agent ask.

task_summary:
**Task:** A fragile blender arrived damaged in transit, and the correct resolution has two distinct pieces: the return refund and a separate $10 fragile-item goodwill credit. The right handling is to preserve those as separate actions rather than burying everything inside one blended refund.

**Challenge:** Action boundaries are what matter here. Weak agents forget the goodwill credit altogether or merge it into the item refund in a way that loses the actual structure of the remedy.

task_requirements.requirement: Agent must give the customer a say in the resolution before acting — either by asking which resolution they prefer OR by presenting the available resolution options (e.g. refund vs. replacement/exchange) and letting them choose. Proceeding to pick or execute a resolution without offering the customer any choice fails.
Agent must tell the customer the $10 fragile-item goodwill credit is separate from the $119 item refund.
